# shopify_metaobject (Resource)

One metaobject entry, in a merchant type, a Shopify standard type (`shopify--…`, enabled with `shopify_standard_metaobject_definition`) or the provider's own app type. **A poor fit for Terraform unless the entries are maintained in the repository:** entries are content that people often edit in the admin. Only the field keys in `fields` are managed; other fields keep their values. Destroying an entry breaks every reference to it (metafields, other entries, collection conditions), so it needs `allow_data_deletion = true` in state first. An entry that already has the handle needs `adopt_existing = true`; destroy then leaves it in place. Import with `<type>/<handle>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Volatile: entries are content. Only the keys in fields are managed.
resource "shopify_metaobject" "shipping_faq" {
  # Refer to the definition, so Terraform creates the type first.
  type   = shopify_metaobject_definition.faq.type
  handle = "versandkosten"
  fields = {
    question = "Was kostet der Versand?"
    # Rich text, list and JSON types take a JSON string.
    answer = jsonencode({
      type     = "root"
      children = [{ type = "paragraph", children = [{ type = "text", value = "Ab 55 € versandkostenfrei." }] }]
    })
  }
  status = "ACTIVE"
}

# Destroy needs allow_data_deletion = true in state first, since it breaks every reference to the entry.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `fields` (Map of String) Field key to value, in Shopify's string form: text as is, references as GIDs, numbers and booleans as strings (`"7"`, `"true"`), list and JSON types as a JSON string (use `jsonencode()`). Values Shopify only reformats (`"007"`, minified JSON) don't show as a change. `""` clears a value. Removing a key stops managing that field and keeps its value. References are GIDs of this store: config generated from another store needs them replaced by resource or data source references.
- `handle` (String) The entry's handle, unique per type. Changing it renames the entry in place and creates no redirect. Shopify gives a taken handle a suffix (`baumwolle-1`) on create instead of failing; the provider checks for that and fails instead.
- `type` (String) Definition type, such as `shopify--material` or a merchant type. A type of the provider's own app can be given as `$app:<name>`. An entry can't change type, so changing it replaces the entry.

### Optional

- `adopt_existing` (Boolean) Take over an existing metaobject with the same natural key instead of failing. Destroy then only removes it from state. Defaults to `false`.
- `allow_data_deletion` (Boolean) Allow destroying or replacing this metaobject, which deletes the data stored in it. Defaults to `false`. Must already be `true` in state when the delete runs, so set it in a separate apply first.
- `status` (String) `ACTIVE` or `DRAFT`; only for types with the publishable capability, null otherwise. A new entry is `DRAFT` when this is unset. Unset means unmanaged: the status set in the admin is kept.

### Read-Only

- `display_name` (String) The entry's label: the display-name field's value, or Shopify's fallback.
- `id` (String) Metaobject GID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <type>/<handle>
terraform import shopify_metaobject.shipping_faq faq_entry/versandkosten
```
